name: 51354-longaudio-omni3b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one vLLM engine.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=8, warmup the first 10% by request count, bounded at 80 requests with a 1800 s safety cap.
workload: Audio understanding over the OpenAI Chat Completions API: one user message per request carrying an eight-word text instruction and one inline base64 `input_audio` part, answered in 16 tokens. Each request carries a distinct ~295 s track, 44.1 kHz stereo, AAC; 80 tracks, none repeated. Transport: POST /v1/chat/completions against a running `vllm serve`.
purpose: An audio question-answering service for full-length music tracks, answering eight concurrent listeners with brief replies on one GPU.
launch:
# The whole launch line is `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B`; everything below is that line plus
# one build-skew workaround. Every other engine setting is the default at this commit.
model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# Not a tuning knob and not part of the declared setup: the venv carries flashinfer-python 0.6.14
# while this checkout's requirements/cuda.txt pins 0.6.16.post3, and the warmup autotune pass
# imports a symbol that does not exist before 0.6.16, so the engine aborts during bring-up. The
# pass runs unconditionally on Hopper whenever flashinfer is importable, even though this
# deployment never dispatches to it.
#
# Spelled as the NEGATED key, and that is load-bearing. This item serves over HTTP, so the config
# reaches the engine through `serving.cli_args`, which renders a bool as a bare FLAG and emits
# NOTHING at all when it is false -- `enable-flashinfer-autotune: false` is silently a no-op and
# the engine still dies. The arg is an `argparse.BooleanOptionalAction`, so `--no-...` is the form
# that sets it False, and `true` here is what makes cli_args emit that flag.
no-enable-flashinfer-autotune: true
